_schema_notes.coverage: Authoritative schema for all DID formats — DD Form 1664 (pre-2014) and free-text (post-2014 MIL-STD-963C)
_schema_notes.did_format: Set to 'dd_form_1664' or 'free_text'. Determines which fields are expected to be populated.
_schema_notes.963c_compliant: True if the DID was prepared under MIL-STD-963C (2014 or later). False for older DIDs.
_schema_notes.reserved_fields: Fields marked RESERVED are present in one format but not the other. Always include them — set to empty string or empty array when not applicable.
_schema_notes.preparation_instructions: Official MIL-STD-963C name for what was previously called 'requirements'. Contains the numbered sections of the DID. All section numbers are normalized to strictly numeric dot-notation (1, 1.1, 1.1.1). Letter-based source numbering (2.a, 3.1.b) is converted to numeric equivalents (2.1, 3.1.2).
_schema_notes.asterisk: True if the requirement number is followed by * in the source document (conditional requirement).

title: Key Specification (KS)
summary: Describes the ordering, generation, distribution, and validation of cryptographic key material for systems and equipment requiring key material, based on the Key and Certification Management Plan.
use_relationship:
The Key Specification (KS) describes the ordering, generation, distribution, and validation of the key material.

a. Key Generation: The KS should designate and describe all types, uses and formats of key required by the application. The KS should also describe the data format, encryption algorithms, parity, checkword algorithms, data constraints, and relationships of one cryptographic application key to another.
b. Key Distribution/Consumption: The KS should describe the type of key and Meta data or fill object the equipment/system will consume. The KS should tailor the mission key and supporting delivery data standards selected from the electronic key delivery references (Electronic Key Management System (EKMS) and Key Management Infrastructure (KMI)) for consumption by the equipment/system based on the Key and Certification Management Plan (KCMP). Note: Over-the-Network Keying is the recommended solution to ensure mission key confidentiality and integrity through distribution and use to ultimate destruction.
c. Key Validation: The KS should contain the results of associated tests to verify that the cryptographic key validation material received agree with the cryptographic key requirements stipulated in the KCMP and KS for the equipment/system. It details the test requirements, describes the tests performed and provides the associated test results and analysis. It is used by the Government to indicate format, function and compatibility acceptance of the cryptographic key software, developed from KS submittal, and resulting key material for use in the equipment/system.
d. This Data Item Description (DID) contains format and content preparation instructions for the data product generated by the specific and discrete task requirement as delineated in the legal agreement, as the KS.
e. This DID is applicable to systems and equipment requiring cryptographic key material.
f. This DID is related to the Tailored Security Design and Analysis Requirements Specification.
g. This DID supersedes prior reference to DI-MISC-80508B titled Technical Report-Study/Services.
distribution_statement: DISTRIBUTION STATEMENT A: Approved for public release; distribution is unlimited.

preparation_instructions.title: Format
preparation_instructions.content: The KS and KS Validation Report Appendix shall:

children.title: Be formatted strictly in accordance
children.content: with the KS and KS Validation Report Appendix Templates established for this purpose and referenced in paragraph 1.5 and 1.6 respectively of this DID, under the "Reference Documents" section.

children.title: Be appropriately classified and portion marked
children.content: in accordance with National Security Agency/Central Security Service (NSA/CSS) Policy Manual 1-52.

children.title: Be submitted in either Microsoft Word
children.content: or Adobe PDF format. Adobe PDF format is preferred as it supports more efficient tracking and management of changes.

children.title: Not contain embedded files
children.content: (i.e. Microsoft Visio drawings). All pictures and diagrams must be converted to a JPG or similar format.

children.title: Include a title page that minimally identifies
Program Manager's name and telephone number and, if applicable, the NSA Cybersecurity Certification Manager's (CSCM's) name and office designator
Include a Revision Page
children.content: listing all past changes to the document in reverse chronological order.

children.title: Include a list of Reference Documents
children.content: This would include all documents used to develop the KS, approved KCMP, and any supporting test validation documentation.

children.title: Include a Table defining all abbreviations and acronyms
Total page count for the KS should
children.content: not exceed 30 pages, with font size and type 12 Times New Roman. NSA reserves the right to return KSs numbering 30 or more pages with instructions to make them more concise and readable.

preparation_instructions.title: Contents
preparation_instructions.content: The KS and KS Validation Report Appendix shall:

children.title: Be completed using the KS Template
children.content: Version 1.0 and the KS Validation Report Appendix Template Version 1.0, included in this DID. NOTE: Not all requested information will apply.
